title: Continuous accountability for Verified bots
summary: Identity alone doesn't guarantee a bot will behave responsibly. We are introducing a system to continuously evaluate whether Verified bots honor site preferences, like robots.txt and HTTP 429s, ensuring they remain accountable over time.

title: Vercel and Shopify make agents first-class shoppers
summary: Agents already shop on the web, but they often use pages and tools originally built for people and search engines. Building a better shopping experience for agents means treating them as first-class shoppers, with product information they can read directly and tools designed for agents to shop.

summary: Cloudflare Gateway and Data Loss Prevention have inherited the flexibility and power of Cloudflare Workers through our full-stack integration with the Cloudflare Developer platform.

summary: For a decade, Vercel has shaped how the web is built. Now, we’re doing the same for agents. The companies that win the next decade will build on infrastructure designed for agents from the start, and thousands of people gathered across London, Berlin, New York, Sydney, and San Francisco to do just that at Vercel Ship…

title: How Vercel Agent accesses production safely
summary: An agent working on production systems needs permission to act. A request like “fix this deployment” doesn’t tell you upfront which actions it will take or what access it will need. Grant agents broad access and a mistake can affect unrelated resources. Ask for approval at every step and the user has to approve…

summary: At Netflix, shared Java libraries support applications developed across a large, independently evolving repository ecosystem. title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
summary: Naive byte-range caching can waste gigabytes of origin bandwidth on small requests. We rebuilt our cache architecture in Pingora to coordinate partial fetches automatically, cutting R2 p99 latency in half.

title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
summary: Cloudflare's new post-quantum GeoKey Manager protects geographically fenced decryption keys from harvest now, decrypt later attacks. Learn how we redesigned our cryptography stack to support strict data sovereignty in a post-quantum world.

summary: Multiple model providers behind one fallback layer with AI Gateway

summary: Put native GitHub features to work to review outside collaborator access and archive stale repositories.

summary: You click play on a Friday night, and in the second that follows, dozens of services answer in milliseconds. Most of them run on Titus, our internal container platform. title: How bug bounty sharpens one researcher’s security skills
summary: As Cybersecurity Awareness Month continues, the GitHub Bug Bounty team spotlights @r31n, diving into their research approach, favorite bug classes, and advice for aspiring hackers.

title: Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
summary: Cloudflare has achieved South Korea's ISMS certification following an audit across 80 controls. Learn how we localized user consent flows, adapted social sign-up paths at the edge, and validated our global security program.

title: Death to long-lived static credentials
summary: Fifteen years ago, TLS was something you'd use to protect the most sensitive areas of your app. Then Google, Let's Encrypt, the EFF, and others led the push for HTTPS everywhere, making encryption the default for every request. Without it, anyone between the browser and server can read and tamper with the traffic.

title: Cloudflare and OpenAI: Making AI discovery better for everyone
summary: How Cloudflare and OpenAI are working together to help AI find useful content, keep up with changes, and make fewer wasted requests — making the experience better for users and website owners alike.

title: Open weight takes 71.5% of tokens and 23% of spend
summary: Every month, AI Gateway routes tens of trillions of tokens between production applications and AI labs. That traffic gives us a view of what AI usage actually looks like in today's enterprise, and we publish it here monthly. See the Production Index reports from July , August , and September .

title: The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure
summary: We moved a copy of 99.99999% of GitHub's repositories to Azure. Here's how per-reference quorums will bring over the rest, and how object storage lets reads scale independently.

title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
summary: Cloudflare's web application firewall can now correlate an HTTP request with its response. Full transaction detection helps every customer find successful exploits, data exposure, and risky misconfigurations that request-only inspection can miss.

title: Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability
summary: Cloudflare has deployed default web application firewall (WAF) protections for newly disclosed PHP vulnerabilities before public disclosure. The rules use request and response signals to stop exploit attempts and prevent exposed data from reaching attackers.

title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
summary: Almost 100,000 Commerce.com domains now give AI agents real shopping tools through WebMCP on Cloudflare. Here's how we turned it on across every store at once, while keeping each merchant in control.

summary: In Part 1 of this series , we shared how Netflix built the Ads Event pipeline and approached it as a system design problem: replacing fragmented pipelines with a centralized collection, enrichment, and a standard data contract. The result was Ads Event Publisher, the system that collects ad telemetry from client…

title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
summary: Following the discovery that eight eMudhra intermediate certificates use weak keys, Cloudflare is deploying mitigations and releasing client updates. We explain the impact, our response, and what customers and developers should do next.

title: How 3 Java Champions are using GitHub Copilot for increased productivity
summary: Three Java Champions share how they use GitHub Copilot to solve problems, accelerate development, and keep humans responsible for the results.

title: Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust
summary: Cloudflare is collaborating on tsrs, a Rust port of TypeScript that is up to 8x faster and uses 70% less memory.

title: Making every harness durable
summary: Developers are familiar with running coding agents locally through harnesses like Pi, Claude Code, and others. They are reliable daily drivers for generating code, but keeping agents running around the clock requires your computer to be on and awake, which led to the laptop lid memes and Mac mini demand spike.

title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase
summary: Learn how to add custom instructions and skills to your repository, use custom agents, and connect MCP servers like Playwright.

title: How one bug bounty researcher chooses the features they investigate
summary: As we kick off Cybersecurity Awareness Month, the GitHub Bug Bounty team spotlights @vaib25vicky, exploring their methodology, techniques, and experiences hacking on GitHub.

title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
summary: When our AI code reviewer's cost per run doubled, we dug into the token usage to find out why. Learn how we used prompt caching and intelligent model routing to slash our inference bill by 68% while speeding up reviews.

title: How to continue a GitHub Copilot app session in VS Code
summary: Learn how to move an agent session from the GitHub Copilot app into VS Code without losing the conversation, code changes, or working context.

title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models
summary: Clairic is a new model from Cloudflare that is a System One extraction modeI, capable of extracting, computing, estimating, and forecasting data from unstructured inputs.

title: Beyond the patch: Protecting your NetScaler gateway against future vulnerabilities
summary: CVE-2026-88771 lets attackers run commands on NetScaler Gateway before anyone signs in. Patching takes time most teams don't have, so the sign-in decision has to move in front of the vulnerable code.

title: Filter, reshape, and redact logs before export with Transformers
summary: Logpush now supports Transformers, allowing teams to filter, redact, and reshape log streams using SQL before export. Powered by Apache DataFusion and Apache Arrow, Transformers apply those changes directly to log data before it reaches the destination.

title: How Rillet ships 3× faster with AI agents on Vercel
summary: Tripled shipping rate in three months with eve agents deployed on Vercel

title: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers
summary: Our new repo star history API now provides trends without returning individual identities or requiring unbounded database work. These are the engineering tradeoffs we made.

title: Inside Hyperdrive: How we solved a rare Hyperdrive MySQL caching bug
summary: While adding MySQL support to Hyperdrive, we found a subtle protocol bug when caching query results. Here is how we tracked down a 0.001% rate error and made Hyperdrive MySQL generally available.

title: Findings from the $1M Vercel Sandbox challenge
summary: In August, we launched the $1M hacker challenge for Vercel Sandbox , inviting security researchers to try and escape Vercel Sandbox. We also coordinated with cybersecurity experts Trail of Bits to review the source code and security architecture.

title: Introducing Clef-omni with full multimodality, plus a faster Clef and a cheaper Clef-flash
summary: We are expanding the Clef decision model family with Clef-omni, natively processing audio, video, images, and text in a single pipeline. We’ve also lowered Clef-flash pricing and boosted Clef inference speeds by up to 2.0x.
